# Guide

The Guide explains the interface and functionality across the produuz.it platform. Use these pages as a reference for each feature area.

## Sections

- **[Viewer](/guide/viewer/)** — The 3D production viewer: visualize designs, track checklists, and manage station workflows.
- **[Management](/guide/management/)** — Company settings, users, projects, production lines, IFC parsing setup, and machines.
- **[Reports](/guide/reports/)** — Generate Bills of Materials, production spreadsheets, quality control reports, QR stickers, and more.
- **[Machine Files](/guide/machine_files/formats/panel_mob1/)** — File formats and machine configurations for CNC equipment (MOB, BTL, XCS, DXF, etc.).
- **[Production Planning](/guide/planning/)** — Schedule constructibles on a calendar with drag-and-drop and workload tracking.
- **[Quantities](/guide/quantities/)** — Plan design quantities across project phases and batches.
- **[Issues Management](/guide/issues/)** — Track production issues and quality control records.
- **[Logistics](/guide/logistics/)** — Material tracking, stock availability, and delivery rack setup.
- **[Stock & Products](/guide/stock/)** — Manage your material catalog: materials, sizes, and products.
- **[Integrations & Webhooks](/guide/integrations/)** — Receive notifications in external systems when events occur.
- **[Account Settings](/guide/account/)** — Personal settings, 2FA, and notification preferences.
- **[API](/guide/api/)** — REST API overview, authentication, and available endpoints.

pages.title: Viewer
pages.body:
# 3D Viewer

The Viewer is the main production interface in produuz.it. It displays 3D models and technical drawings of your constructibles (assemblies and modules), and provides tools for managing production checklists, issues, logistics, and more.

[[toc]]

## Accessing the Viewer

You can open the Viewer from the constructibles list in a project. There are two viewing modes:

- **Actual Viewer** — For constructibles in production. Includes checklists, issues, RFID, and logistics features.
- **Design Viewer** — For reviewing designs before production. Shows 3D models and drawings in read-only mode (no production tools).

## The list on the left

The left menu holds the queue: every constructible you can work on, in the order production follows. What sits above that list depends on how you are working.

### Working by date

With no project selected, and if your company works by date, the header shows the **date selector**: arrows for the previous and next day, and a dropdown with a calendar and two options — whether to include constructibles that are late, and whether to cap how many are listed at a time.

### Working by project

With a project selected, the header shows one control for everything that decides what the list holds. Closed, it tells you where you are:

- the phase on the top line and the batch on the bottom one, or *All phases* / *All batches* when nothing is filtered;
- how many constructibles of what is listed are ready, out of the total;
- an eye icon crossed out when ready constructibles are being hidden;
- a `×` to clear the filter in one tap.

The arrows step to the previous and next batch, continuing into the next phase when you reach the end of one.

Tapping the button opens it:

- **Production / Design** at the top, for managers and admins. Production lists the panels and modules being built; Design lists the designs, read-only. In Design mode there are no batches, so the phase and batch list is not shown.
- Tap a **phase** to see its batches only.
- Tap a **batch** to work on that batch alone.
- Every row shows how many of its constructibles are ready. The count turns green once they all are, so a finished batch or phase is easy to spot. Batches with nothing in them are greyed out and never count as finished.
- The switch at the bottom hides constructibles that are already finished. It stays open while you use it, so you can compare.

The constructible you currently have open always stays in the list, even when the filter would leave it out, so you never lose your place.

## Layout

![Viewer Layout](./viewer_layout.png)


The Viewer uses a three-panel layout:

| Panel | Content |
|-------|---------|
| **Left** | 3D model or technical drawing (PDF) |
| **Center** | Vertical toolbar with action buttons |
| **Right** | Part details (BOM) or specification documents |

There are two views, switched with the chevron button at the top of the toolbar:

- **Extended** — All three panels. The right panel shows the panel checklist at the top and the usual drawing underneath, so a worker can tick tasks off with the drawing in front of them. The checklist button is not in the toolbar in this view: it would only open the same tasks in a dialog.
- **Standard** — Left panel + toolbar. The drawing takes all the width, and the checklist goes back to being a button in the toolbar.

Extended is the default on big screens, standard on phones, and your choice is remembered on that device. Both views are available on any screen: on a phone the two panels stack and share the height instead of sitting side by side.

## 3D Model

![3D Model](./viewer_3d.png)

### Controls

- **Rotate** — Click and drag to rotate the model.
- **Zoom** — Scroll wheel or double-click to zoom in.
- **Pan** — Right-click and drag to move around.
- **Recenter** — Click the crosshair button to reset the view.
- **Front/Back** — Toggle buttons to flip the camera perspective.

### Selecting Parts

Click any part in the 3D model to select it. The right panel will show its properties, including:

- Zone and reference number
- Material type and dimensions
- IFC properties and property sets
- Creation date and revision number

### Zone Selection

Use the zone toggle buttons to show or hide specific zones of the constructible. This is useful for focusing on a specific area during production.

For modules, you can also filter by sub-assembly using the assembly dropdown.

### Advanced Tools

- **Measurement** — Click the ruler icon to measure distances between parts in the 3D view.
- **Clipping Plane** — Click the section icon to enable a cutting plane that reveals the interior structure.

![Clipping Plane](./viewer_clipping.png)

## Technical Drawings

![Technical Drawings](./viewer_drawings.png)

The left panel can switch between the 3D model and technical drawings (PDFs). Use the buttons at the bottom of the left panel to select which drawing to display.

- Drawings are filtered by your selected production station when applicable.
- Multi-page drawings show navigation arrows to move between pages.
- Zoom and pan controls work the same as in the 3D view.

## Bill of Materials (BOM)

![Bill of Materials](./viewer_bom.png)

The right panel in **Details** mode shows the Bill of Materials for the current constructible.

### Part List

A table listing all tracked parts with:

- Reference number
- Part category badge
- Specifications
- Zone location

Use the **branch filter** buttons (e.g., wood, metal, hardware) to show only parts from a specific construction branch.

### Unknown Parts

A separate tab shows parts detected in the IFC file but not matched to the database. This helps identify parts that may need to be added to the system.

### Part Drawings

When a part is selected, you can view its associated detail drawings and CAD files in the right panel.

## Production Features

::: info
Production features are only available in the **Actual Viewer** (not in Design Viewer).
:::

### Checklist

![Checklist Dialog](./viewer_checklist.png)

The checklist button in the toolbar shows the production progress for the current constructible at the selected station.

- **Progress bar** — Color-coded: red (not started), amber (in progress), green (completed).
- **Task list** — Each task has a checkbox, and may require:
  - QR code scanning
  - A picture (see below)
  - Filling a custom form
  - Reviewing associated documents

**Tasks that need a picture**

The task row has a **camera button** and a **browse button**, on every device.

- On an Android tablet or phone, the camera button opens the device's own camera
  app: take the photo, confirm, and you are back on the checklist.
- On a computer or a Windows tablet it opens the camera in a small window — one
  click to open, one to shoot.
- The browse button picks a photo you already have. On a computer you can also
  drag files onto the row or paste a screenshot into it.

::: tip The camera button opens the gallery instead?
Some companies manage their tablets with a policy that blocks the camera app.
The app cannot tell that apart from a working camera, so it asks and the device
answers with the photo gallery. Switch on **Avoid native camera in viewer** in
*Company → Viewer settings* and the app will take the picture itself instead of
asking the device.
:::

- The photo is stored **exactly as the camera took it**, at full resolution. It
  is the quality record of the panel, so nothing is shrunk or re-compressed.
- **The task ticks itself** when the photo is stored, as long as nothing else is
  missing — a form still to fill or a QR still to scan keeps it unticked. You can
  always untick it.
- The photos stay visible **after** the task is ticked, as thumbnails. Tap one to
  see the picture full size. **Clean** removes them. A photo taken before this
  feature existed gets its thumbnail the first time somebody opens the panel, so
  an old panel with many pictures fills in over a couple of visits.
- Each thumbnail says **who uploaded it**. See:
  [Quality Control Report](/guide/reports/quality_control/)
- If the upload fails you get a message, the thumbnail disappears and the task is
  **not** ticked, so a missing photo can never look like a stored one.

**Actions:**
- **Start Production** — Begin work on this station (required before checking tasks).
- **Pause** — Temporarily stop work.
- **Station Job Completed** — Mark the station as done (enabled when all tasks are checked).

### Multiwall Checklist

When you open a Multipanel Group in the viewer, the toolbar shows a Multiwall Checklist button instead of (in addition to) the per-panel one. It aggregates the checklist of every member panel of the group at the currently selected station, so a worker can drive the whole multiwall from a single screen.

- **Progress** — The button shows how many panels of the group are loaded and the combined progress for the current station across all of them.
- **Simple tasks** — A single checkbox represents the task across the group. Clicking it asks whether to apply the change to **all panels** or to **just one** (and which one). The chip on the right shows how many panels already have it ticked (`3 / 5`).
- **Tasks with a picture, form or QR field** — These are expanded into one row per panel, each labelled with the panel name, so the operator can fill the picture/form/QR for each panel individually.
- **Station switcher** — The same station-switching control as the per-panel checklist is available in the dialog header to move the whole group between stations.

### Station Switching

Click the station button to change to a different production station. If previous stations haven't been completed, you'll be asked to confirm a force-start.

### Issues

![Issues Dialog](./viewer_issues.png)

The issues button shows a badge with the count of active issues for this constructible.

- **View issues** — See all issues with their title, description, category, status, and attached pictures.
- **Add issue** — Create a new issue with a category, title, description, and optional picture upload. You can attach the current part information for context.

### QR Code

Click the QR button to display a QR code for the current constructible. This can be printed and attached to the physical item for quick identification on the shop floor.

### RFID Tag

Click the RFID button to register an RFID tag code for the current constructible. You can type the code manually or scan it using the camera.

### Rack / Logistics

The rack button shows whether the constructible has been loaded into a delivery rack.

- **Load to Rack** — Mark the item as placed in a rack.
- **Unload from Rack** — Remove the rack assignment.
- Shows a visual representation of the rack arrangement.

## Specifications & Documents

Switch to the **Docs** mode in the right panel to view specification documents associated with the constructible. These may include finish specifications, hardware specs, or other technical documents in PDF or image format.

pages.title: Properties in Texts
pages.body: # Properties in texts Several text fields in Produuz.it are **templates**: you type free text, and wherever you want a value from the model you write a property name between curly braces. ``` Project: {project_name} - Phase: {phase_name} ``` becomes ``` Project: Zonnehof - Phase: Fase 2 ``` Every field that works this way has an **Insert property** button ({ }) on its right. It lists everything you can use in that field, including your own model properties, and inserts it where the cursor is. That button is the authoritative list — this page is the same list, written down. [[toc]] ## Where you can use them | Where | Field | Resolved per | |-------|-------|--------------| | Company → Viewer settings | **Custom Viewer Header** | Panel | | Company → Viewer settings | **Custom List Hint** (the second line in the viewer list) | Panel | | Company → Viewer settings | **Custom Constructibles Table Column** | Panel | | Machine setup → BTL / BTLx / BVX | **Part data fields** (Designation, Assembly number, Group, Package, Material, Timber grade, Quality grade, Subgroup / Storey) | Part | | Machine setup → BTL / BTLx / BVX | **User attribute values** (up to 5) | Part | The two groups use **two different lists**, because they are resolved against two different things. A viewer header describes a panel; a BTL Designation describes one piece of timber inside that panel. Read the right table below. ## Panel properties Used by the viewer header, the list hint and the custom constructibles column. | Property | Value | |----------|-------| | `{design_name}` | Design name of the panel | | `{priority}` | Priority inside the batch | | `{batch_name}` | Batch name | | `{phase_name}` | Phase name | | `{scheduled_prod_date}` | Scheduled production date | | `{client_order_id}` | Client order id | | `{project_name}` | Project name | | `{project_number}` | Project number | | `{super_project}` | Super project | | `{client_name}` | Client name | Plus **your own properties** — see below. ## Part properties Used by the machine file fields (BTL, BTLx and BVX). These are resolved **per part**, so a single file covering a whole batch still carries the right panel name on every piece. | Property | Value | |----------|-------| | `{part_pos}` | Part reference / position | | `{name}` | Part name | | `{material}` | Material | | `{description}` | Part description | | `{erp_mat}` | ERP material code | | `{comment}` | Comment | | `{finish}` | Finish | | `{width}` / `{height}` / `{length}` | Dimensions | | `{unit}` | Unit | | `{profile_size}` | Profile size | | `{shaped_section_name}` | Shaped section name | | `{zone}` | Zone | | `{assembly_name}` | Panel name | | `{design_name}` | Panel name — the same value as `{assembly_name}` | | `{batch}` | Batch name | | `{phase}` | Phase name | | `{project_name}` | Project name | | `{project_number}` | Project number | | `{super_project_name}` | Super project | | `{client_order_id}` | Client order id | Plus **your own properties** — see below. ::: tip The panel names also work here `{super_project}`, `{batch_name}` and `{phase_name}` — the names the panel list above uses — are accepted in machine file fields too, and give the same value as `{super_project_name}`, `{batch}` and `{phase}`. You do not have to remember which list you are in. ::: ## Your own properties Both lists also accept **any property of your own models**. These are the keys stored on a panel as client metadata: whatever your IFC parsing setup extracts, or whatever your ERP writes through the API. They are different at every company — `{montagevolgorde}` is a real property at one company and a typo at every other. Two ways to see yours: - The **Insert property** button lists them under *Your own properties*. It is read from your own panels, so if the section is empty it means none of your panels carry properties of their own — not that the list failed to load. - On any panel: **Constructibles → open the panel → Client meta**. ## Rules - **A property that does not exist is not an error.** In the viewer settings it renders as `---`; in machine files it renders empty. Nothing fails, so a typo is silent — which is exactly why the Insert property button exists. - **Free text is kept as it is.** `Order {client_order_id} - {design_name}` gives `Order ORD-88 - HD-529`. - **Every property must be named.** `{}` and `{0}` are not accepted, and the field will say so before you can save. - **Every brace must be closed.** `{design_name` is rejected the same way. - **To print a literal brace**, double it: {{ gives `{`. - **Numbers can be padded**: `{priority:03d}` gives `007`. This only works on numeric properties. - **Your own properties cannot override the ones in the tables above.** If one of your model properties is called `design_name`, `{design_name}` still means the design name.

pages.title: Management
pages.body:
# Management - Company Settings

<!-- [[toc]] -->

In the company settings view, company managers and admins can tweak several settings.

## Main settings

### Company info

Company info such a as address, name and email are shown on reports, mails and other templates. Company notifications are sent to the "contact email".

### Interface settings

* Show QR button: Show a button in the panel viewer that gives the user a QR for the panel.
* Show RFID button: Show a button in the panel viewer that gives the option to register RFID tags.
* Hiding parts in the 3D viewer is no longer a company setting. It is a **custom part class** in your parsing setup: give the class the rules that recognise those parts and turn on *Hide in the 3D viewer*. That way each setup decides for itself, instead of one switch deciding for the whole company. See: [Custom part classes](/guide/management/ifcps/#custom-part-classes)
* Show project number in the project selector: Adds the project number above the project name in the project selector, and next to the project name in the views that list projects from several projects at once. The number is left out when the project name or the superproject already starts with it. With this on, the selector also gets a search box that matches name, number and superproject.
* Language: This is the default language for the app. Users can change the language if they are allowed by the admin (see the Users table).

## Licenses

Gives a main overview of the licensing.

## Styles

Corporate color and logos can be changed. Those will be used also in PDF generation. Sticker banner is a wide logo to be used in some of the sticker presets (like panel QR stickers).

Once you pick a corporate color it is used across the interface (buttons, links, scrollbars) and in PDF generation. If you prefer the standard produuz.it orange in the interface, untick "Use corporate color" next to the color picker — the color is kept and still used in PDFs.

## Projects

Projects are fabrication sets that we recommend don't get more than 100 designs and 500 panels for performance reasons. The more panels in a project, the slower the interface gets.

We know that there are some large or very large projects that doesn't fit on those numbers, so we introduced the "superproject" parameter, so you can group several projects under the same key name. For example, you may have a big project with 10 buildings, and you may want to split it into 10 projects that belong to the same superproject.

Projects can be "archived" 🗃. Archived project are hidden from the user, and only visible in the archive. We plan a feature to export all the information of an archived project in a .zip file.

Each project can have an **engineering contact** — the person to reach with questions about it, typically the responsible engineer. In the project form (and in Project Settings), pick an existing contact or create a new one on the spot. Once set, it is shown to production staff in the issue detail panel (see [Contacts](#contacts)).

## Users

### User form

* 🌐 **Multilanguage**: User can change language of the interface.
* 👁 **Hide panel queue**: If checked, can see only designs mode in the viewer, not the panel list.
* 🔃 **Can change station**: User can change him/herself to other station.
* 🌴 **Has own holydays**: If checked, user doesn't get the company holydays. System only takes own holydays.
* 🔨 **Has own worktime**: If checked, own entries have priority over company entries. This means that if you set a worktime with start and end date, all days outside this range will take company worktime.

::: info Work Calendar
More about holydays and worktime in [Work Calendar](#work-calendar)
:::


## Contacts

Contacts are people to reach about a project, such as the responsible engineer. A contact has a name, phone and email, and is **not** a system user.

Manage them in the **Contacts** table, below Users. You can also add a contact directly from the project form when assigning one.

A project can have an **engineering contact** (set in the project form or in Project Settings). When it does, that contact is shown to production staff in the issue detail panel, so they know who to reach with questions about an issue.


## Machines

Machines represent CNC equipment or automated stations in your production lines. Each machine has a model type (e.g., Mobi One) and a configuration that defines how machine files are generated.

To set up machines, go to **Company Settings > Production Lines** and configure them under the machines section. Machines are linked to specific stations in your production line.

::: tip
For details on configuring production lines, stations, and machines, see the [Production Lines](/guide/management/production_lines/) reference page.
:::

## Work Calendar

The work calendar controls how production time is calculated across the system. It defines working hours and holidays at both the company and user level.

- **Company holidays**: Default holidays that apply to all users.
- **Company worktime**: Default working hours (start/end times per weekday).
- **User-level overrides**: Individual users can have their own holidays and worktime entries (configured in the Users form with the "Has own holidays" and "Has own worktime" checkboxes).
